LanguageData.CC_Settings_EnableWishes_Tip: Colonists voice wishes based on their traits, passions, relationships and mood.

LanguageData.CC_Stakes_Gentle_Tip: Only upsides. Granted wishes and achieved ambitions lift mood; ignoring a wish, refusing it or failing an ambition costs nothing. Trust is still tracked, but only its good side has effects. Bad quirks are off; decrees still cost some mood, at half strength, because you chose them.
LanguageData.CC_Stakes_Balanced_Tip: Upsides and downsides. Ignored wishes and refusals sting, broken promises sting more, colonists who waited longer feel passed over, the jealous resent favorites, and ignored colonists can turn disgruntled and work slower. Granted wishes can leave people motivated.
LanguageData.CC_Stakes_Demanding_Tip: Like Balanced, with every penalty 50% stronger. Bitter, unhappy colonists may storm off to sulk or go on an insulting spree.
LanguageData.CC_Stakes_AdvisorOnly_Tip: No mood effects from this mod at all. Wishes and ambitions are pure suggestions.

LanguageData.CC_Settings_ForOthers_Tip: A kind colonist may notice someone else's hardship and ask for them. Both are happier if it's granted.
LanguageData.CC_Settings_Petitions_Tip: Colonists who want the same thing back each other's wish instead of making a new one.

LanguageData.CC_Settings_MeetingsCallFromWork: Meetings call people from their work
LanguageData.CC_Settings_MeetingsCallFromWork_Tip:
When a council meeting starts, the chair calls everyone over. Colonists put down ordinary work and walk to the meeting, and sleepers are woken (and grumble about it). No colonist is pulled from urgent work such as tending, rescues, surgery, firefighting or feeding, and children, the sick and the worn out are left to sleep.

Turned off, colonists come only when they are free, as they would for a party.

Either way, the letter says who came, who was late and who missed it.

LanguageData.CC_Settings_Standards: Rising standards: the happy grow harder to please
LanguageData.CC_Settings_Standards_Tip: While colonists are happy, their standards creep up: the council's mood rewards shrink, letdowns sting more, and wishes come more often and ask for more. Hard times, and the austerity decree, bring standards back down.
LanguageData.CC_Settings_StandardsComforts_Tip: Rising standards also shrink the good moods from the base game and other mods, not only the council's: comfortable colonists feel them at 90%, particular ones at 80% and spoiled ones at 70%. Only the first 10 points of each count for less, so a wedding or a catharsis still lands. Bad moods are never touched. One of the deeper game hooks.
LanguageData.CC_Settings_GoodTimes_Tip: A colonist whose mood is already above 75% keeps Rimfolk's new good memories for less time, down to half their usual time from 90% mood. In hard times good things last their full length, and how good they feel never changes. One of the deeper game hooks.
LanguageData.CC_Settings_SmallJoys_Tip: Every good mood Rimfolk gives a colonist (a wish granted, a wedding, a dilemma that went their way, a reunion, a feast) shares one budget: the two biggest on their mind count in full, the next ones a half, a third and a quarter, and every one after that a fifth. Each stays on the Needs tab at what it counts for now. Bad moods, and everything the game and other mods give, are left alone.

LanguageData.CC_GoodTimes_Tip:
How a good life turns ordinary, without taking anything away:

Getting used to good times: from 75% mood, Rimfolk's new good memories fade sooner, in half their usual time from 90%. In hard times they last their full length.

Good moods add up slowly: of the good moods Rimfolk gives, the two biggest count in full, the next ones a half, a third and a quarter, and every one after that a fifth. Many small moments give something else instead of mood (recreation, rest, practice, trust).

Standards and comforts: comfortable colonists feel the good moods of the game and other mods at 90%, particular ones at 80% and spoiled ones at 70%, on the first 10 points of each.

Bad moods are never touched. Each rule has its own setting.

LanguageData.CC_Social_Intro: Who is close to whom, who can't stand whom, and who is teaching whom. Bonds grow out of how people feel about each other and what they go through together. They shape votes, objections, petitions and elections.
LanguageData.CC_Social_None: No lasting bonds yet. They form over time, through shared work, fights and hardship.
LanguageData.CC_Social_CliqueTip: A circle: three to six people held together by strong friendships. They back each other's wishes and petitions and vote together.
LanguageData.CC_Social_TieTip_Trust: Bonds sway the council: friends back each other's wishes and petitions, rivals object to each other's, and both count in elections.
LanguageData.CC_Settings_Dreams_Tip: Colonists sometimes wake from a dream: about what happened that day, the people in their lives, the dead they miss, or something still to come. Most are just a mood and a line in their journal (hover the mood to read the dream). Now and then one leaves an inspiration, a lesson, a changed feeling about someone, or a wish.
LanguageData.CC_Settings_DreamOmens_Tip: Rarely, a dream is an omen: a visitor, a trader, a newcomer, a storm or a raid, and a few days later it happens. At most one omen waits at a time.
LanguageData.CC_Settings_AllDreamMessages_Tip: Off: only dreams that change something get a message; the rest are in the journals, the mood tooltip and the Dreams page. On: every dream.
LanguageData.CC_Dream_CameTrue: {PAWN_nameDef}'s dream came true. Days ago {PAWN_pronoun} woke up saying: "{DREAM}"

LanguageData.CC_Social_DreamsNone: Nobody has told of a dream yet.
LanguageData.CC_Settings_Aspirations_Tip: After settling in, each colonist sets their heart on something to do before they die: master a craft, marry, raise a child, earn a name, teach someone everything they know, see the colony grow. Achieving it is a big moment (a lasting good mood, trust, maybe an inspiration). Dying before achieving it is mourned.

LanguageData.CC_Settings_Secrets_Tip: Some colonists carry a secret, often from their past: a raider's life, noble blood, a child left behind, a debt, a hidden kindness. They may confide in a close friend (you'll only see that they did). Friends can let it slip, rivals will, and when it comes out everyone reacts according to their nature. Sometimes the council has to decide what to do about it.
LanguageData.CC_Settings_Vendettas_Tip: When raiders kill or carry off someone, the people who loved them swear vengeance on that faction: a weight they carry, fury when that faction attacks again, satisfaction when enough of them fall, and outrage if the council makes peace with the killers.
LanguageData.CC_Settings_Eulogies_Tip: When a colonist dies, the person closest to them speaks at the grave, in their own voice.

LanguageData.CC_Settings_Quirks_Tip: Colonists pick up beliefs and habits from what they live through: a lucky helmet after surviving a raid in it, a dread of storms after a death, a ritual before every fight, prayers at night after a dream came true. Small moods at the right moments, and they fade in time.
LanguageData.CC_Settings_Heirlooms_Tip: When a colonist dies, their weapon or hat passes to the person who loved them most. Carrying it is a comfort (to anyone, more to the heir); losing it hurts.
LanguageData.CC_Settings_ComingOfAge_Tip: When a child grows up, the colony marks it, and the council helps choose their path: an apprenticeship with the colony's best, the defenses, or their own way.
LanguageData.CC_ComingOfAge_Text: {PAWN_nameDef} is grown. The child who ran between the buildings is an adult now, with a say at the council and a life to choose.

LanguageData.CC_Settings_Presets_Tip: Start from one of these, then fine-tune on the other pages.
LanguageData.CC_Settings_EraNoGame: The era is set per colony: load a game to change it. Every colony starts on Auto, which recognizes a medieval or tribal colony by its research and buildings.
LanguageData.CC_Era_Auto_Tip: The mod reads your finished research and your buildings to decide what your colony can make. Works for most games, including modded tech trees.
LanguageData.CC_Era_PreIndustrial_Tip: Treat the colony as pre-industrial whatever the research says: no power, turrets, freezers or solar flares in advice, wishes, dreams and text. For medieval playthroughs.
LanguageData.CC_Era_Industrial_Tip: Treat the colony as industrial or later even if the research looks primitive (useful with tech trees the mod can't read).
LanguageData.CC_MsgLevel_Everything_Tip: A message for every dream, small social moment, quirk and confidence. Busy, but you won't miss a thing.
LanguageData.CC_MsgLevel_Notable_Tip: Messages for what changes something: bonds formed, vendettas, secrets out, names earned, dreams that mattered. The small moments are still in the journals, the Story tab and the History section.
LanguageData.CC_MsgLevel_LettersOnly_Tip: Only letters and the biggest moments (an omen coming true). Everything else is in the council window.
LanguageData.CC_Settings_Encounters_Tip: Small moments between colonists and everyone else on the map: news from visitors, haggling with traders, words through a prisoner's door, a fallen raider's plea, a pet's mischief, a stag at dawn. Also turns on the council's choices about strangers (a visitor who wants to stay, a trader who wants an heirloom).
LanguageData.CC_Settings_Nemeses_Tip: An enemy who strikes down, maims or kills a colonist and gets away is remembered. A wild animal that does it gets a name. The one they hurt feels it until it's settled: captured, killed, or never seen again.
LanguageData.CC_Settings_NemesisReturns_Tip: A raider who got away sometimes rides with their people's next raid (at most three times).
LanguageData.CC_Settings_PetMoments_Tip: An animal that fights beside its person in a battle is remembered for it, and a named animal that dies gets a farewell from the one who loved it. People talk to the animals they work with, a bonded animal follows its person about, births in the herd are news, and the herdmaster names the newborns.

LanguageData.CC_Settings_Character_Tip: The council's choices add up to a reputation: merciful or harsh, generous or thrifty, traditional or restless, open or guarded, hard-working or easygoing. Colonists approve or chafe by nature, neighbors hear of it, and some encounters and dilemmas only come up for a colony with a certain name. Old deeds slowly fade.

LanguageData.CC_Ways_Renowned: The colony is renowned as {0}. Travelers talk about it wherever they stop, and the colonists hear it said of them.
LanguageData.CC_Ways_Meaning_Mercy_Pos: Kind souls are proud of it; the bloodthirsty think the colony has gone soft. Desperate strangers may come looking for sanctuary.
LanguageData.CC_Ways_Meaning_Mercy_Neg: The bloodthirsty approve; kind souls are troubled by it. Some will think twice before crossing the colony, and some will never trust it.
LanguageData.CC_Ways_Meaning_Generosity_Pos: Kind and simple souls approve; the greedy grumble. Neighbors warm to the colony over time, and those in need remember it.
LanguageData.CC_Ways_Meaning_Generosity_Neg: The greedy approve; the kind find it mean. Neighbors cool toward a colony that keeps everything for itself.
LanguageData.CC_Ways_Meaning_Tradition_Pos: The old are glad of it; the young find it stifling. Customs and celebrations matter more here.
LanguageData.CC_Ways_Meaning_Tradition_Neg: The young love it; the old miss how things were. Old habits get dropped and new ones tried.
LanguageData.CC_Ways_Meaning_Openness_Pos: Kind and sociable souls approve; the abrasive don't. Neighbors warm to the colony, and more strangers stop by.

LanguageData.CC_Settings_Moments_Tip: Colonists share small moments in conversation: grieving together, talking shop, praising the cook, telling old stories, friendly contests. They show in the social log, and as speech bubbles with Interaction Bubbles.
LanguageData.CC_Settings_Frictions_Tip: The small irritations of living close together, like dishes left in the basin, a snoring bunkmate or advice nobody asked for. A messy or cramped home brings its own, like a leaking roof, a sticking door or a smoky room. Each costs a point or two of mood for half a day to a day and a half. A tidy, roomy colony has far fewer of them.
LanguageData.CC_Settings_Life_Tip: Everyday pressures a well-run colony has to keep up with, like the same meal again and again, the same work for days, someone dear away for long, a packed dining or rec room, or half-built work left standing. Each is small, says what causes it and what helps, and goes away once that's dealt with. A varied table gives a small lift. The same setting covers setbacks in the colony's life: work wrecked or torn down, a crop lost, a friend fallen ill, a feast that ran out.
LanguageData.CC_Life_Gentle_Tip: Pressures at half strength, never less than 1. Half-built work isn't minded, and high standards don't make the colony's small frictions sting more.
LanguageData.CC_Life_Normal_Tip: Pressures as designed, 1 to 3 mood each. Spoiled colonists feel them, and the colony's other small frictions, up to 40% more.
LanguageData.CC_Life_Demanding_Tip: Pressures half again as strong, for colonies that stay content too easily.

LanguageData.CC_Settings_WorldReactions_Tip: Weddings, births, homecomings from long journeys and friends breaking down leave journal lines, a line in the chronicle when it matters, and small moods (glad you're back, home again). Needs the deeper game hooks.
LanguageData.CC_Settings_WorldEvents_Tip: Rimfolk's own events: colonists' pasts catching up with them (old comrades, lost family, creditors, bounty hunters, news from home), challenges (a traveling champion, a legendary beast, a treasure map, a demand for tribute), wonders and nuisances of the land, neighbors who want something, and visitors with a purpose. Many follow up on earlier ones. Each fits the colony's era, and many touch Rimfolk's other systems: nemeses, secrets, mentors, the colony's character. Dev mode can fire any of them (Debug actions, incidents, "Council_Evt_..."). The bigger happenings across the whole region are world events, with their own switch below.
LanguageData.CC_Settings_EventsFromStoryteller_Tip: On: Rimfolk's events join your storyteller's own random events and follow its rhythm, quiet spells and threat cycles; the ones that can end in a fight go in with its small threats. Off: they come on Rimfolk's own timer instead, and never take a slot from the storyteller.

Only when the storyteller sends threats at all, never on top of another fight, and at a share of the storyteller's own raid strength. Off: none of these come (and promised fights never arrive).

LanguageData.CC_Scen_LetterIntro: The colony didn't start with a clean slate.
LanguageData.CC_Scen_NoEnemy: Whoever this colony crossed, there's nobody in this world hostile enough to come after it.
LanguageData.CC_Scen_Foe_hunts: {FOE_nameDef} of {FACTION} has sworn to hunt down {VICTIM_nameDef}, and has the people to do it.
LanguageData.CC_Scen_Foe_robbed: The silver was taken from {FOE_nameDef} of {FACTION}, and {FOE_nameDef} knows exactly who took it: {VICTIM_nameDef} planned the job.
LanguageData.CC_Scen_Foe_betrayed: {FOE_nameDef} turned the crew against {VICTIM_nameDef}, and has friends among {FACTION} down here.
LanguageData.CC_Scen_Foe_enslaved: {FOE_nameDef} of {FACTION} held {VICTIM_nameDef} and the others in chains for years.
LanguageData.CC_Scen_Foe_Prisoner: Now {FOE_nameDef} is the colony's prisoner, and {FACTION} will want {FOE_objective} back.
LanguageData.CC_Scen_Foe_Once: They'll come for the colony once, before long.
LanguageData.CC_Scen_Foe_Again: They'll come for the colony before long, and a couple more times after that, unless {FOE_nameDef} falls first.
LanguageData.CC_Scen_Foe_Always: They'll come for the colony before long, and keep coming every so often for as long as {FOE_nameDef} lives.
LanguageData.CC_Scen_Debt_loan: The colony owes {FACTION} {AMOUNT} silver, the price of everything it landed with. They'll want it in about {DAYS} days.
LanguageData.CC_Scen_Debt_heist: The {AMOUNT} silver in the colony's packs belongs to {FOE}, by any reasonable account. {FACTION} will come asking for it in about {DAYS} days.
LanguageData.CC_Scen_Deserters: {NAMES} deserted from {FACTION}. Their old unit still has their names, and is still looking.
LanguageData.CC_Scen_Families: The {NAMEA} family: {FAMILYA}. The {NAMEB} family: {FAMILYB}. The two families have never gotten along.
LanguageData.CC_Scen_SecretHint: Not everyone here is telling the whole truth.
LanguageData.CC_Scen_HuntWarning: Word comes that {FACTION} are on the move, and coming this way. They'll be here within hours.
LanguageData.CC_Scen_Hunt_hunt_Text: {FACTION} are coming for the colony again, on {FOE}'s word.
LanguageData.CC_Scen_Hunt_hunt_Led_Text: {FOE} has found the colony again, and leads a war party of {FACTION}.
LanguageData.CC_Scen_Hunt_hunt_Captive_Text: {FACTION} have come to take {FOE} back from the colony, by force.
LanguageData.CC_Scen_Hunt_mutiny_Text: {FACTION} have sent their people after the colony again, on the orders of {FOE}, the mutiny's ringleader.
LanguageData.CC_Scen_Hunt_mutiny_Led_Text: {FOE}, the mutiny's ringleader, is leading {FACTION} against the colony in person. Whatever happened on that ship, {FOE} means to finish it here.
LanguageData.CC_Scen_Hunt_heist_Text: {FACTION} have come for the money again, on {FOE}'s orders, and this time they mean to take it by force.
LanguageData.CC_Scen_Hunt_heist_Led_Text: {FOE} still hasn't been paid back, and has come to collect in person, with {FACTION} behind.
LanguageData.CC_Scen_Hunt_tyrant_Captive_Text: {FOE}'s loyalists of {FACTION} have come to break their master out, and to punish the ones who rose up.
LanguageData.CC_Scen_Hunt_tyrant_Led_Text: {FOE} is free, and has come back at the head of {FACTION} to take back the valley, and the people {FOE} still thinks of as property.
LanguageData.CC_Scen_Hunt_loan_Text: {FACTION} have come to collect what the colony owes them, one way or another.
LanguageData.CC_Scen_HuntOver_dead: {FOE} is dead. {FACTION} have no reason left to come for the colony, and the hunt is over.
LanguageData.CC_Scen_HuntOver_gone: {FOE} is gone, and with {FOE} went the reason {FACTION} kept coming. The hunt is over.
LanguageData.CC_Scen_HuntOver_joined: {FOE} is one of the colony now. Strange as that is, it means {FACTION} have stopped coming.
LanguageData.CC_Scen_HuntOver_enslaved: {FOE} wears the colony's collar now, and with no one left to follow, {FACTION} have stopped coming.
LanguageData.CC_Scen_HuntOver_peace: {FACTION} have made peace with the colony. Whatever {FOE} wants, {FACTION} won't be fighting for it anymore.
LanguageData.CC_Scen_HuntOver_defeated: {FACTION} are no more, and the hunt died with them.
LanguageData.CC_Scen_HuntOver_gaveup: {FACTION} seem to have given up on the colony. {FOE} is still out there somewhere, but the attacks have stopped.
LanguageData.CC_Scen_HuntOver_settled: {FACTION} have taken what they think they're owed out of the colony's hide. As far as they're concerned, the debt is settled.
